source: PF1e potion-able 1st-3rd level spells, converted by hand against content/spells/spells.json.
note:
A curated conversion, not a bulk one. content/spells/spells.json holds 3,040 spells as PROSE ONLY — no structured effects — so every entry here was read and encoded by hand, and every `spell` id is verified to resolve in that file (tests/test_alchemist.py asserts it). A potion of a spell the app has never heard of is the 'ground every name' failure CLAUDE.md records, so the id is the contract: `Result.output['holds_spell']` carries it, and a potion holding spell X stands in for knowing spell X.

Caster level is 1e's minimum for the spell level — CL 1 for a 1st-level spell, CL 3 for a 2nd, CL 5 for a 3rd — and every duration and die below is that caster level already worked out, because a card that says 'minutes/level' makes the player do arithmetic the bench already knows the answer to.

What the effectspec vocabulary cannot hold stays `narrative`, never a guessed spec. Two cases recur: an effect the drinker chooses the target of (lesser restoration mends 'one ability score of your choice' — picking one here would invent a fact the spell never gave), and effects with no counterpart in the engine's vocabulary at all (gaseous form, water breathing). Those are recorded and narrated, which is honest; a spec that looks authored and does nothing is worse.

Materials are the spell's own printed material component wherever 1e prints one — enlarge person is brewed with the powdered iron the spell itself calls for. The medium sets the tier and therefore the level gate: rectified spirits or font water (uncommon) for 1st-level potions, a rare catalyst for 2nd, azoth (exotic) for 3rd.

potions.name: Potion of Enlarge Person
potions.text: The pinch of powdered iron the spell itself calls for, taken up in spirits and reacted until the solution will not sit still in the vial. It grows the drinker a size category: everything that follows from being bigger, including the parts that are not an improvement.

effects.target: size category increases by one; space becomes 10 ft and natural reach 10 ft, and equipment grows with the wearer

potions.name: Potion of Reduce Person
potions.text: The same working run backwards, with talc where the iron would be. Smaller, quicker, harder to hit and markedly less use in a doorway.

effects.target: size category decreases by one; space becomes 2-1/2 ft and natural reach 0 ft, and carried gear shrinks along

potions.name: Potion of Cure Light Wounds
potions.text: Font water and a styptic salt, reacted until the vial is faintly warm to hold. The first potion any bench learns and the last one any party stops buying.

potions.name: Potion of Mage Armor
potions.text: A scrap of finished leather dissolved to nothing at all — what the working wants is the idea of armour, not the hide. An hour of protection that weighs nothing and makes no noise.

effects.note: as an armour bonus — it does not stack with worn armour

potions.name: Potion of Shield of Faith
potions.text: One line of scripture on vellum, dissolved until the ink is a grey thread in the water and then not even that. What is left turns blades a hand's breadth from the skin.

potions.name: Potion of Protection from Evil
potions.text: Powdered silver in font water — the ward every hedge-priest draws, drunk instead of chalked. It leans against evil specifically and does nothing whatever about a falling rock.

effects.note: against effects created by evil creatures
against effects created by evil creatures
against effects created by evil creatures

effects.target: blocks mental control and bars bodily contact by summoned creatures

potions.name: Potion of Remove Fear
potions.text: Camphor's sharpness cutting through font water: it clears the head the way cold air does. Whatever was already frightening the drinker stops working the moment it goes down.

potions.name: Potion of Jump
potions.text: The spell's own grasshopper legs, steeped and reacted out. A minute in which gaps stop being arguments.

potions.name: Potion of Longstrider
potions.text: A pinch of road dust, which is the component the spell asks for and a joke the trade never tires of. An hour of covering ground.

potions.name: Potion of Expeditious Retreat
potions.text: Shaved licorice root in spirits, reacted hot and corked while it fizzes. Named honestly: it is for leaving.

potions.name: Potion of Endure Elements
potions.text: Camphor and embalmer's salt: one keeps the head cool and the other refuses to let the body lose water. A full day of weather being somebody else's problem.

effects.target: the drinker exists comfortably in conditions between -50 and 140 degrees Fahrenheit without needing to make Fortitude saves

potions.name: Potion of Comprehend Languages
potions.text: Soot and salt, which is what the spell prints and what the trade has always used. Ten minutes in which every inscription in the room is suddenly addressed to you.

effects.target: the drinker understands any spoken or written language they hear or touch, though it does not decode ciphers or secret writing

potions.name: Potion of Pass without Trace
potions.text: Mistletoe cut with bronze and never allowed to touch ground, dissolved in spirits. A plant that owes the earth no footprint, lending the habit out for an hour.

effects.target: the drinker leaves no tracks, trail or scent; tracking them by any mundane means is impossible for the duration

potions.name: Oil of Magic Weapon
potions.text: Powdered lime and carbon in spirits — the spell's own components — wiped down a blade rather than swallowed. The steel takes an edge it did not have and keeps it for a minute.

potions.name: Oil of Magic Fang
potions.text: For the companion rather than the sword: rubbed into claw, horn or tooth. Cheap, quick, and the difference between a bite that lands and one that glances.

effects.note: one natural weapon of the anointed creature
one natural weapon of the anointed creature

potions.name: Potion of Cure Moderate Wounds
potions.text: Font water stirred with alicorn until the shaving comes out no lighter than it went in. The horn is a catalyst in the strict sense: it does the work and is not spent.

potions.name: Potion of Bull's Strength
potions.text: A few hairs from a bull's shoulder — the spell asks for exactly that and no more — carried by philosopher's wool into something the body will accept.

potions.name: Potion of Cat's Grace
potions.text: A pinch of fur, combed and not pulled. Nothing lands better than the animal it came off, and for three minutes neither does the drinker.

potions.name: Potion of Bear's Endurance
potions.text: Oily guard hairs from a winter coat. The animal sleeps through half a year of hunger; the draught borrows the part of that which is stubbornness.

potions.name: Potion of Eagle's Splendor
potions.text: Two clean pinions, reduced to nothing in the flask. What comes out is bearing — the drinker is not better looking, they are harder to dismiss.

potions.name: Potion of Fox's Cunning
potions.text: Red guard hairs from the ruff. The trade has never found a better sympathy for thinking sideways, and has stopped looking.

potions.name: Potion of Owl's Wisdom
potions.text: Soft-edged feathers that fly silent. Three minutes of knowing better, which is not the same as being told.

potions.name: Potion of Barkskin
potions.text: Oak bark taken without ringing the tree, reduced until the flask smells like a wet wood in autumn. The skin roughens and does not soften again for half an hour.

potions.name: Potion of Invisibility
potions.text: Gum arabic holding the suspension together — the spell's own binder, doing the same job in a bottle that it does in a gesture. The classic, and the one every party buys two of.

effects.note: while invisible and moving; +40 while invisible and holding still

effects.target: the drinker and their carried gear become invisible; attacking or casting an offensive spell ends it immediately

potions.name: Potion of Blur
potions.text: Mithral dust suspended in gum until the flask itself is hard to focus on. Cheaper than invisibility and harder to argue with, because it does not end when you swing.

effects.target: the drinker's outline wavers: all attacks against them suffer a 20% miss chance, and it does not end when they attack

potions.name: Potion of Resist Energy (Fire)
potions.text: Salamander ash, which remembers being fireproof, lending the memory out for half an hour. Swap the elemental reagent — winter wolf humour, everfrost salt — and the same chain retunes to cold.

potions.name: Potion of Darkvision
potions.text: An agate polished thin enough to see a candle through, dissolved past seeing. Three hours in which the dark is simply a room with the lamps off.

potions.name: Potion of Delay Poison
potions.text: Aloes bitter enough to teach a lesson, in font water. It does not cure a poisoning — it tells the poison to wait, and poison, for three hours, waits.

effects.target: poison already in the body is suspended rather than cured: when the draught expires, the remaining duration resumes where it left off

potions.name: Potion of Lesser Restoration
potions.text: Alicorn and font water, which is the oldest answer in the book to being diminished. What it mends is whichever score is hurt worst — the drinker chooses as they swallow.

effects.target: heals 1d4 points of temporary ability damage to a single ability score, chosen by the drinker as they swallow

potions.name: Potion of Spider Climb
potions.text: Bitumen and a live spider, exactly as printed, and the spider is released afterwards by any alchemist worth drinking with. Half an hour of walls being floors.

effects.target: the drinker climbs walls and ceilings with their hands free, and need not make Climb checks to do it

potions.name: Potion of See Invisibility
potions.text: Talc and powdered silver, the two things that have always shown up what is not there. Half an hour of the room being honest with you.

potions.name: Potion of Aid
potions.text: The plainest divine draught there is: courage and a cushion. The temporary hit points are the part people remember at the wrong moment.

potions.name: Potion of False Life
potions.text: Salt out of a crypt cistern, which is cold on the tongue and colder afterwards. It lends a margin that was never the drinker's; when it goes, it goes all at once.

potions.name: Potion of Remove Paralysis
potions.text: Smelling salts with a benediction behind them. Poured between the teeth of somebody who cannot ask for it, which is the only way it is ever used.

effects.target: frees one creature from magical paralysis, hold or slow; a creature that is merely staggered is unaffected

potions.name: Oil of Align Weapon (Good)
potions.text: Silver and font water, wiped down the blade with a rag that is burned afterwards. Three minutes in which the sword argues on the right side of a demon's hide.

effects.target: the coated weapon counts as good-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction

potions.name: Potion of Cure Serious Wounds
potions.text: Azoth is the solvent that is also the medicine, and alicorn is the catalyst that is never spent. Together in a crystal retort they make the best draught the mundane trade can honestly sell.

potions.name: Potion of Fly
potions.text: A wing feather in azoth — the spell's own component, in the only solvent that will take it up whole. Five minutes, which is either plenty or catastrophically few.

effects.target: flight with good manoeuvrability; when the draught expires the drinker falls, so the last round is spent landing

potions.name: Potion of Haste
potions.text: Licorice root driven through azoth until the retort will not stop humming. Five rounds — brief on purpose, because the alternative is a preparation nobody can price.

effects.note: one extra attack at full bonus when making a full attack

potions.name: Potion of Heroism
potions.text: Temple-forged sunmetal, warm in the hand at midnight, taken up by azoth. Nearly an hour of being the version of yourself the story needs.

effects.target: the same +2 morale bonus applies to every skill check the drinker makes

potions.name: Potion of Water Breathing
potions.text: A hollow reed cut below the waterline, which carries air through water as a plain fact before the chain makes a subtler one of it. Ten hours, and it divides among everyone who shares the flask.

effects.target: the drinker breathes water freely for ten hours; the duration divides evenly among all creatures who share a single dose

potions.name: Potion of Gaseous Form
potions.text: Gauze and smoke resin, which is what the spell prints, in the one solvent that will hold a thing while it stops being solid. The classic answer to a locked door and a bad plan.

effects.target: the drinker and their gear become insubstantial smoke: fly 10 ft (perfect), pass through small holes and cracks, immune to poison and critical hits, and unable to attack, cast with somatic components or use most items

potions.name: Potion of Neutralize Poison
potions.text: Where delay poison tells the venom to wait, this one ends the conversation. Charcoal and aloes doing what they always do, with azoth making them mean it.

effects.target: detoxifies any venom in the creature: poison currently affecting them ends, and they cannot be poisoned again for the duration

potions.name: Potion of Protection from Energy
potions.text: A bank against one element rather than a wall: it absorbs, keeps count, and stops the moment the account is empty. The elemental reagent chosen at brewing decides which element it argues with.

effects.target: absorbs up to 60 points of damage of one energy type — acid, cold, electricity, fire or sonic, fixed when the potion is brewed — and ends early once that total is spent

potions.name: Oil of Keen Edge
potions.text: Star-iron in azoth, wiped down the edge with the grain. The steel does not get sharper so much as more willing, and the difference shows up in the crits.

effects.target: doubles the threat range of the coated slashing or piercing weapon; it does not stack with any other effect that widens a threat range
